title: voice lab compact prioritization and impact notes
content:
Purpose: compact synthesis from last 6 weeks of CS intake (calls, support threads, in-product flags) — create a minimal set of prioritized asks and short impact/effort notes to route to product/eng owners.

Context and signal summary (high-level):
- Recurring themes: cost visibility per-route, predictable latency under burst, improved dev ergonomics for model pinning and fallbacks, finer-grained caching controls for enterprise workloads.
- Volume: ~120 unique ask threads (May–Jun 2028); ~30 high-intensity customers generating ~65% of operational risk signals.
- Severity: 8 P1-ish tickets tied to SLA breaches (timeouts under burst; poor fallback behavior), many P2 feature requests for observability and routing controls.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We can't calibrate our prompts if we don't see token cost split by model and route — it's a black box." (large fintech)
- "During Black Friday-esque spikes our app throttles; fallback to cheaper models causes hallucination regressions and product incidents." (ecommerce platform)
- "We want a simple knob to say: keep latency < 200ms for checkout flow even if that costs 2x per-token." (marketplace)

Clustered asks and proposed quick categorization:
1) Cost & observability (high frequency, medium effort)
   - Per-route / per-invocation token cost breakdown (hosted API consoles & SDKs). Impact: high (reduces billing disputes, improves adoption). Quick win: add per-request cost metric to usage logs + console filter. Owner: product-hosted-api + console.
   - Token source attribution (prompt vs. completion vs. functions). Impact: medium. Effort: low.

2) Routing & SLO controls (high impact, higher effort)
   - Policy-level routing: rule to route sensitive routes to dedicated pools or to cheapest compatible model under cost cap. Impact: very high for enterprise. Effort: medium-high (routing infra + UI). Owner: eng-platform-engineering + product.
   - Explicit per-route latency SLO with automatic fast-fallback option (prefer lower-latency variant, not just cheaper). Tradeoff: requires model profiling and latency SLAs per region.

3) Caching & batching controls (medium frequency; technical complexity)
   - KV/prefix controls surfaced to customers (TTL, sizing hints) + suggested config presets by workload. Impact: medium-high (can reduce unit cost). Owner: serving-runtime + optimize.
   - Workload-aware batching presets (small, medium, background) exposed in SDK. Effort: low-medium.

4) Private / compliance asks (lower frequency but high contract value)
   - Auditable per-tenant logs for private deployments, tie to KMS events. Impact: high for regulated customers. Effort: medium. Owner: private-deployments + security-and-compliance.

5) Developer ergonomics (many small asks)
   - API to pin model version per-route + rollout controls (canary percentage, time windows). Impact: medium. Effort: low.
   - CLI/SDK helper to simulate cost/latency on a sample prompt set before rollout. Effort: low.

Cross-cutting risk notes and tradeoffs:
- Any UI that surfaces cost needs to align with billing backend (avoid mismatch). Short-term: show estimates tied to model profiles; long-term: reconcile with final invoice.
- Fast fallback policies reduce downtime but create quality regressions — need gated rollout and fallbacks that prefer compatible architecture/quantization family rather than arbitrary cheaper model.
- Exposing caching internals: customers will tune aggressively; ensure defaults protect multi-tenant memory and enforce limits on private vs hosted.

Quantitative impact heuristics (quick RICE-like thinking for triage):
- Per-route cost visibility: reach 60% of enterprise customers; expected to reduce billing disputes 40%. Estimated effort: 2–3 sprint slices.
- Routing policies/SLOs: unlocks larger deals for enterprise; prevents major incidents during spikes. Estimated effort: 3–6 sprints cross-team.
- KV controls and presets: 15–25% token savings on chat-heavy workloads when tuned. Estimated effort: 2–4 sprints.

Suggested short-term roadmap (owner handshake + next steps):
- Week 0–2: engineering discoverys (ENG-5123) to validate logging surface required for per-request cost lines. Owner: Miguel (platform eng) + Claire (console PM). Output: minimal logging schema + sample console widget mock.
- Week 2–6: ship per-invocation cost estimates in usage logs + console filter (beta with 5 customers). Owner: product-hosted-api.
- Parallel: prototype a routing rule PoC that accepts: route id, latency cap, fallback preference. Small internal test using 2 customers. Owner: eng-infra. (linked ticket: CS-2419)

Fast proposals for micro-patches (can ship in 1 sprint each):
- Add "estimated_cost_usd" field to request logs + SDK mapping (1 sprint).
- Add a console toggle to show/hide token split columns and download CSV (1 sprint).
- Default batching preset "interactive-small" to reduce latency for low-token chats (1 sprint).

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve in discovery):
- How to attribute function-call tokens reliably across multi-tool responses? (needs infra validation)
- Should fallback policies be allowed to change model family (quantized vs fp16)? What are CV/contract implications?
- How to couple cost estimates with billing to avoid mismatches and disputes?

Customer champions and priority list (top 8 callers):
- Fintech A (high willingness to pay for per-route SLOs)
- Marketplace B (latency-sensitive checkout flow)
- Enterprise SI C (requires audit logs for private deployment)
- Ecomm D (spike behavior: wants immediate fallback control)
- Healthcare E (compliance + KMS integration)
- Analytics SaaS F (wants per-invocation token split)
- EdTech G (cost-savings via batching/caching presets)
- Gaming H (streaming/low-latency variant requests)

Decision record (proposed, needs alignment):
- Prioritize per-request cost visibility as near-term bet (low effort, high customer ROI, reduces friction).
- Begin routing SLO discovery in parallel but treat as second wave (requires infra/time).
- Bundle caching presets with "Optimize" playbook content for customers (docs + console templates).

Next logistics / meeting asks:
- Quick sync (30m) with console PM, platform eng lead, SRE to align logging schema — target: Tues 2028-06-26.
- Demo slot request with 3 anchor customers for beta on cost-visibility (Jul week 2).

Notes to self:
- Capture sample CSVs from billing team to validate token attribution mapping.
- Add a short tech appendix for ENG-5123 with field list and sample events.

Appendix: sample support thread excerpts (redacted)
- "We're seeing 2–4x token variance on identical prompts after we switched to new model family — need breakdown per-call."
- "Fallback picked a 4-bit quantized model that halved cost but caused hallucinations in billing summary."

End of notes.

(Will iterate after discovery sync; this doc is intentionally compact to hand off to product owners.)
